key_insight: In turbulent pipe flow with azimuthally non-uniform heating, the global Nusselt number is essentially unchanged by the azimuthal heat-flux pattern and only weakly affected by solid properties, but the local temperature field and fluctuations remain strongly shaped by conjugate heat transfer at low Prandtl number.
engineering_relevance: Designers of liquid-metal and other low-Prandtl-number cooling systems can rely on robust overall heat-transfer performance while still accounting for strong local thermal nonuniformity caused by the pipe wall and heat-flux distribution.
method: Spectral decomposition of arbitrary azimuthal heating into discrete wavenumbers.
Well-resolved thermally and hydraulically fully developed turbulent pipe-flow simulations.
Comparison across Pr = 0.025 and 0.71 with varying solid thermal properties and effusivity ratio K.
evidence_signal: The study combines theory with numerical simulations at Re_tau ≈ 180 and reports that the global Nusselt number is independent of azimuthal heat-flux distribution, while local mean temperature and fluctuations depend on wavenumber and solid coupling.
watch_item: The results are obtained for thermally and hydraulically fully developed flow at moderate Re_tau, so extrapolation to higher Reynolds numbers, transients, or strongly developing inlet conditions should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Conjugate heat transfer in turbulent pipe flow with azimuthally non-uniform heating
